content:
This July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be welcomed with open arms, but the same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't significantly affected by this bug. Because of that, I initially thought the TestFlight update was a simple but meaningful improvement.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta apps when it comes to Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds "a search bar to quickly find apps."

In retrospect, I did notice some oddities, which I noted at the bottom of my article (though my understanding at the time was completely backwards):

I think the reason I didn't realise this was a bug is because I held onto years' worth of TestFlight beta apps in order to "merge" what had originally been separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It's not the most convenient arrangement, but for me it was worth it.

Regardless, the TestFlight bug did not escape the notice of MacStories' John Vorhees:

So, when I saw Zac Hall's piece at 9to5Mac about TestFlight gaining a search bar, you can imagine my excitement. I thought, "Finally!" I immediately dropped what I was doing and updated the app. [...] Unfortunately, there's a big "but" to this story. In the past, TestFlight beta versions were listed in reverse chronological order, which I personally loved. [...] Now, those expired beta versions are mixed in alphabetically with currently active TestFlight betas, and the expired beta list appears to have expanded to include every single beta I've ever been part of. I did a quick count, and for me it's nearly 800 app entries. As you can imagine, very few of those are actually active betas. The search feature does help, but scrolling is no longer a viable way to find anything.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote at Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was raised by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. While the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update did indeed fix the bug in question.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix for users affected by this regression.
